comparison: Perfect agreement on iPSC generation and characterization (C25-C30). Both evaluations find the reprogramming, pluripotency markers, karyotyping, and isogenic controls well-supported and crucial for study validity.

Both support iMac generation and functional characterization (C31-C36). OpenEval finds comprehensive validation; peer review accepts phagocytic capability but notes incomplete protein-level characterization and requests additional validation via flow cytometry/ELISA.
Agreement on reduced CSF-1 sensitivity (C37-C38). Both evaluations accept this finding as consistent with expected HDLS pathophysiology and supported by MTT assay data.

Agreement on metabolic reprogramming findings (C2, C48-C54). Both evaluations support the glycolytic shift and metabolic changes, with peer review explicitly identifying this as a strength confirmed across both patient lines.

Divergence on transcriptomic data (C39-C47). OpenEval finds comprehensive support despite noting missing statistical details; peer review rates as uncertain, requesting combined analysis of both lines, overlapping GO terms, and protein-level validation.

Agreement on IL-1β upregulation and inflammatory phenotype (C4-C5, C56-C58). Both evaluations support the transcriptional findings as providing mechanistic insight, though OpenEval notes lack of protein-level confirmation.

Both address phagocytic capacity (C55). OpenEval includes this with inflammatory phenotype findings; peer review treats it separately as functional characterization. Both accept the finding without challenge.

Divergence on microglial differentiation (C59-C66). OpenEval supports acquisition of microglia-like characteristics despite limited sample recovery; peer review rates as uncertain, questioning morphology evidence and requesting better imaging and highlighting of core microglial genes.

Partial overlap on organoid co-culture effects (C67-C68). OpenEval rates overall findings as uncertain due to inconsistencies; peer review supports the specific neuronal population changes with statistical evidence.

Overlap on organoid transcriptomic changes (C69-C71, C82). OpenEval includes these in uncertain evaluation of overall organoid results; peer review supports these specific findings as evidence for microglia-neuron interactions.

Both address cholesterol-related findings (C80-C81). OpenEval includes these in uncertain evaluation noting lack of cholesterol measurement; peer review supports the finding with appropriate caveats about need for further characterization.

Agreement on overinterpretation of mechanistic claims (C6-C8). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting lack of direct causal demonstration; peer review also uncertain, with explicit request to tone down arguments about microglial dysregulation and IL-1β contribution.
Both address inflammatory state interpretation (C78-C79). OpenEval includes in uncertain mechanistic model evaluation; peer review supports this as consistent with cytokine data and HDLS pathology.

Agreement on speculative nature of mechanistic proposals (C83-C84, C86). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting model is plausible but lacks causal demonstration; peer review also uncertain, noting these extend beyond what data support.
Agreement on therapeutic speculation (C87). OpenEval rates as unsupported with no experimental data; peer review includes in uncertain evaluation of speculative proposals that extend beyond evidence.
Agreement on limitations of prior models (C20-C24, C72-C73). Both evaluations support these claims as establishing rationale and novelty of the iPSC approach with isogenic controls.

Agreement on iMac yield variability (C74-C76). Both accept the observational findings; OpenEval notes speculation about mechanisms; peer review acknowledges variability as limitation without disputing observations.
Agreement on baseline cytokine elevation (C77). OpenEval supports based on qPCR data; peer review also supports as consistent with reactive phenotype, though requests protein validation.
